newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says member states may decide public body not taxable.
newsitem.headline: Court says member states may decide public body not taxable.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday member states may characterize public authorities as non taxable persons, even where they perform activities generally taxable for private persons.
Under the Sixth VAT directive, public authorities are not considered taxable persons, unless to not do so would lead to a significant distortion of competition, the court said.
Article 13 of the directive provides that the leasing and letting of immovable property is exempt from VAT, but that taxable persons may choose to be taxed.

Under German law, the leasing of real estate by a public body is treated as a taxable event only if as lessor, the public body also instals and provides any equipment required to run the commercial activity on the premises. Otherwise, the activity is considered to be asset management only.
In this case, a German municipality challenged the Finance Court's characterization of it as a non-taxable person as it sought to recoup VAT paid to erect the building.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Sixth VAT directive - Letting of immovable property - Public authority"
Reference from the Bundesfinanzhof (Germany) for a preliminary ruling between

on the interpretation of article 4(1), (2) and (5) and article 13(B) and (C) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

The fourth subparagraph of article 4(5) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment, must be interpreted as permitting member states to consider that the activities listed in article 13 of the directive are carried out by bodies governed by public law as public authorities, even if they are performed in a similar manner to those of a private trader.
